name: SEC EDGAR (US Securities and Exchange Commission full-text search, XBRL/company facts APIs, and filing archives)
hq_country_operator: United States - operated by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (federal government agency)
data_types: Full corporate disclosure filings (text + structured XBRL financials) including 8-K (Item 1.01 material definitive agreement, Item 2.01 completion of acquisition/disposition), S-4 (merger registration statements), SC TO-T and SC TO-I (tender offers), SC 14D9 (subject company tender offer response), SC 13D/13G (beneficial ownership, often M&A-precursor stakes), DEFM14A/PREM14A (merger proxy statements), Form 425 (merger communications), 10-K/10-Q financials, and XBRL company facts/concepts/frames (structured financial statement data).
coverage_geo: US-listed public companies and foreign private issuers that file with the SEC (includes many non-US companies cross-listed in the US, but not purely domestic-Japan companies)
history_depth: EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) indexes filings since 2001, confirmed directly from SEC's own EFTS FAQ page (date-range presets include 'All (since 2001)'). Full filing archives (non-full-text, via full-index files) go back to EDGAR's inception in the early-to-mid 1990s. XBRL structured data (companyfacts/frames) is only available for periods after XBRL mandates took effect (roughly 2009 onward, phased in by filer size).
api: yes - multiple REST/JSON APIs, no API key/auth required: (1) EDGAR full-text search at https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=... returns JSON hits with filer, form type, date, CIK; (2) data.sec.gov submissions API at https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json (per-company filing history/metadata); (3) XBRL companyconcept, companyfacts, and frames APIs under https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/. Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces and https://www.sec.gov/os/webmaster-faq#developers. Rate limit confirmed from SEC's own developer FAQ: maximum 10 requests/second, and a declared User-Agent header is mandatory (format 'Sample Company Name AdminContact@domain.com') - undeclared/generic user agents are blocked. No official technical support is offered for programmatic/scripted access ('We do not offer technical support to programmatically download filings').
bulk_delivery: yes - nightly bulk ZIP files: companyfacts.zip (all XBRL company facts) and submissions.zip (all company filing history/metadata), both republished nightly around 3am US Eastern time per SEC's own API documentation page. Also daily and full (quarterly) index files (form.idx, company.idx, master.idx) under https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/full-index/ listing every filing since EDGAR's start. Separate 'Financial Statement Data Sets' (structured financial statement extracts) are also published, referenced in the SEC developer FAQ.
pricing: free - no cost, no API key, no registration required for any of the above (confirmed via SEC's own API docs and developer FAQ, fetched 2026-09-03). Only a compliant User-Agent header and adherence to the 10 req/sec rate limit are required.
ml_training_license: SEC.gov content is US federal government work product; SEC's own privacy/site-use guidance (per web search of sec.gov/about/privacy-information and related pages) states site content is public information that may be copied/redistributed without SEC permission, with attribution to SEC as source recommended. No explicit clause addressing AI/ML model training was found on any fetched SEC page. Inference: because EDGAR filings are US government works, they are not subject to US copyright domestically, which strongly suggests no legal barrier to using them for AI training, but this was not stated verbatim by SEC and should be confirmed with legal counsel given JCAI's Japan-based use case and any cross-border considerations.
language: English (filings occasionally include foreign-language exhibits for foreign private issuers, but the vast majority of content and all metadata are English)
update_frequency: Near real-time: submissions API updates typically within under 1 second of a new filing being accepted per SEC's own API docs; XBRL data APIs update within about 1 minute; full-text search index and bulk ZIPs (companyfacts.zip/submissions.zip) refresh nightly (~3am ET).
fit_for_lead_prediction: Strong for training M&A-target-prediction models on US/cross-border deals: 8-K Item 1.01/2.01, S-4, SC TO-T/14D9, SC 13D and DEFM14A/PREM14A filings directly label real M&A events with dates, parties, and deal terms, and can be paired with XBRL pre-deal financials (companyfacts) as predictive features. ETL effort is moderate-to-high: full-text search and submissions APIs return filing metadata/links but the actual deal terms (price, structure, target/acquirer identification) require parsing filing text/HTML (8-K item text, S-4/proxy bodies) since these are largely unstructured narrative documents, not tagged XBRL facts; building a clean labeled M&A-event dataset needs custom NLP/regex extraction plus dedup/entity-resolution across CIKs.

name: EDINET (Electronic Disclosure for Investors' NETwork) API v2, Japan Financial Services Agency
hq_country_operator: Japan - operated by the Financial Services Agency (金融庁), a Japanese government agency
data_types: Statutory Japanese corporate disclosure documents including 臨時報告書 (extraordinary reports - the primary near-real-time disclosure of M&A/share transfer/business transfer events), 有価証券報告書 (annual securities reports, full financials), 半期報告書/四半期報告書 (semi-annual/quarterly reports), 公開買付届出書 (tender offer registration statements) and related tender offer response documents, and 大量保有報告書 (large shareholding reports, incl. amendment/correction reports - early signals of accumulating stakes, often M&A precursors). Data available as XBRL (structured, for financial-statement-bearing documents), PDF, and CSV (for some report types).
coverage_geo: Japan-listed and other FSA-regulated/disclosure-obligated companies (issuers filing under Japan's FIEA); does not cover unlisted/private Japanese companies unless they have public debt or other disclosure triggers
history_depth:
CORRECTION (2026-09-03, verified against FIEA Art. 25 via e-Gov and EDINET API spec v2.9): extraordinary reports are viewable 5 YEARS (not 1 year; 1 year applies to the treasury-stock repurchase report). Annual / semi-annual / quarterly reports 10 years; tender-offer filings 5 years from end of offer period; 5% reports 5 years; list API accepts dates back 10 years. Original researcher text follows.

Materially shorter and more fragmented than SEC EDGAR, and varies sharply by document type - confirmed via web search of Japanese sources describing EDINET's 縦覧期間 (statutory public-viewing period) plus 延長期間 (administrative extension period): 有価証券報告書 and 半期報告書 total 10 years (5-year statutory + 5-year extension); 四半期報告書 also totals 10 years (3-year statutory + 7-year extension); 公開買付届出書 (tender offer filings) are viewable for 5 years after the tender offer period ends; 大量保有報告書 (large shareholding reports) for 5 years from receipt. Critically, 臨時報告書 (extraordinary reports - the document type that most directly discloses M&A/business-transfer events) has only a 1-year public viewing period after receipt, after which it is no longer viewable on EDINET at all. This means real-time API pulls or a scheduled archiving pipeline are necessary to build a durable historical M&A-event dataset from EDINET; the API alone cannot retrieve most M&A-triggering extraordinary reports older than about 1 year.
api: yes - REST/JSON, EDINET API v2, documented in the FSA's official 'EDINET API 仕様書 (Version 2)' PDF (dated as recently as June 2026 per search results at https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/guide/static/disclosure/download/ESE140206.pdf, though the PDF itself could not be parsed as text via WebFetch - binary/image content). Two main endpoints found via search: documents.json (list API, e.g. https://api.edinet-fsa.go.jp/api/v2/documents.json?date=YYYY-MM-DD&type=...&Subscription-Key=...) for per-day document lists, and documents/{docID} (acquisition API) for retrieving a specific document's content/attachments. Requires an API key passed as a 'Subscription-Key' parameter, obtained via a self-service signup portal (redirects to an Azure AD B2C login/registration flow at fsaedinetauth.b2clogin.com, confirmed via direct fetch). Rate limiting: search results indicate a required ~1 second interval between requests for bulk/asynchronous retrieval, with API keys subject to temporary suspension if this is violated; exact numeric SLA was not found in machine-readable form (the authoritative spec PDF could not be text-extracted in this research pass).
bulk_delivery: No dedicated bulk-download ZIP/dataset product was found (unlike SEC's companyfacts.zip/submissions.zip). Bulk historical retrieval is effectively done by scripting repeated documents.json calls per date across the available viewing-period window; this is the community-documented pattern (per Japanese developer blog posts found in search, e.g. Zenn articles on scripting EDINET pulls), not an officially provided bulk file.
pricing: free - API key registration is free of charge (confirmed via multiple Japanese search sources), requiring only an email address and phone number for signup; no paid tier was found for the official EDINET API itself. (Note: distinct third-party commercial services such as edinetdb.com/sec-api-style wrappers exist and charge for convenience/aggregation, but the official FSA EDINET API is free.)
ml_training_license: EDINET content is governed by Japan's public data terms of use, specifically stated (via direct fetch of the official 利用規約 page at https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/guide/static/submit/WZEK0030.html) to follow 'Public Data Utilization license (PDL 1.0)' (公共データ利用規約). Under this, reuse/redistribution and editing/processing of content is permitted provided the source is attributed (e.g. 'created by [Company] based on EDINET viewing/submission site [URL]') and any modification is disclosed. No explicit prohibition on commercial use was found in the fetched summary, but the source recommends checking the full PDL 1.0 text directly. No explicit clause on AI/ML training use was found - the fetched terms-of-use summary states this is simply not addressed. Scraping (スクレイピング) of the EDINET site itself is explicitly prohibited, but use of the official API is explicitly carved out as an exception. ml_training_license: unknown for the AI-training-specific question; permissive for general reuse/redistribution with attribution.
language: Japanese (primary; document text, form labels, and XBRL taxonomy element names are Japanese). Some large-cap issuers voluntarily file English-language disclosure documents (英文開示) but this is a minority of filings.
update_frequency: Documents become available via the API as they are received/accepted by EDINET, i.e. same-day/intraday during business days; the documents.json list API is queried per calendar date.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Moderate fit, with an important caveat: 臨時報告書 (the best real-time M&A/business-transfer disclosure signal) is only viewable for 1 year, so building a multi-year labeled training set requires either (a) an ongoing daily scheduled scrape/archive job run prospectively from today forward, or (b) sourcing historical extraordinary reports from a third-party archive/paid data vendor, since the official API cannot retrieve most of them retroactively beyond ~1 year. 有価証券報告書/半期/四半期 financials (10-year depth) are well suited as structured XBRL features for a target-company financial profile, and 大量保有報告書 (5-year depth) can serve as an M&A-precursor signal. ETL effort is moderate: JSON list + document fetch is straightforward, but XBRL parsing (Japanese taxonomy) and extracting deal-specific facts from 臨時報告書 free-text/PDF requires custom Japanese-language NLP work.

name: GLEIF LEI Data (Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation)
hq_country_operator: Switzerland (Basel) — GLEIF is a non-profit foundation established by the Financial Stability Board / G20 to operate the Global LEI System.
data_types: LEI reference data Level 1 ('who is who': legal name, registered/headquarters address, legal form, registration authority, entity status, LEI issue/renewal/lapse dates, following LEI-CDF 3.1 format) and Level 2 Relationship Records ('who owns whom': direct parent and ultimate accounting-consolidating parent relationships between LEI-holding entities), plus Reporting Exceptions files (documents cases with no parent, opt-outs, or parents lacking an LEI, with a stated exception reason/category). Also LEI-to-ISIN, LEI-to-BIC, and LEI-to-OpenCorporates-ID mapping/relationship files.
coverage_geo: Global — legal entities that have registered for an LEI, concentrated in regulated/financial-market-participant entities and their corporate group structures worldwide (LEI is mandated for parties to many financial transactions/reporting regimes in EU, US, and elsewhere). Coverage skews toward entities involved in financial markets rather than a full census of all companies; historically weaker for non-financial mid-market Asian companies unless they are financial-market counterparties or have voluntarily obtained an LEI.
history_depth: LEI system operational since 2014 (post-2008-financial-crisis G20/FSB initiative); historical records go back to each entity's LEI registration date, not to company founding date. Total LEI population: active LEIs surpassed 3 million in Q1 2026 (~3.02M active, +3.4% QoQ), with active+lapsed population over ~3.26M by Q1 2026 and 320M+ [likely a typo for records count, reported as '3.2 million+'] by Q3 2026 per GLEIF blog figures.
api: yes - REST, JSON:API format. Public docs via Postman collection at https://documenter.getpostman.com/view/7679680/SVYrrxuU (redirected from api.gleif.org/docs); could not extract endpoint/rate-limit detail directly from the Postman page content via WebFetch. Per secondary sources, rate limit is 60 requests/minute/user (429 returned when exceeded); no API key/authentication required for the public LEI Search API.
bulk_delivery: Yes - 'Golden Copy' full-population files published 3x daily, standardized and duplicate-free, in LEI-CDF 3.1 format, with 4 delta files per publication covering changes from the prior 8 hours, 24 hours, 7 days, and 31 days. Also available via RDF format through a data.world partnership. Exact native file formats (XML/JSON/CSV) for Golden Copy were not explicitly enumerated in the fetched page beyond the LEI-CDF/RDF references — Inference: LEI-CDF is XML-based per prior GLEIF format history, with CSV/JSON concatenated files also offered elsewhere on gleif.org (per GLEIF Concatenated Files pages found in search, not independently fetched). Separate mapping files: BIC-to-LEI (CSV, monthly, produced with SWIFT), ISIN-to-LEI, and OpenCorporates-ID-to-LEI relationship files also downloadable.
pricing: Free. All Golden Copy, delta, relationship, exception, and mapping files, plus the public API and Global LEI Index search, are provided at no cost (per gleif.org/en/lei-data pages and gleif.org/en/about/open-data, observed 2026-09-03).
ml_training_license: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero / public domain dedication) — confirmed via GLEIF's 'Open Data' and terms-of-use pages (secondary-source summary: 'data on the GLEIF website is made available under a Creative Commons (CC0) licence'). CC0 imposes no attribution or share-alike restriction, so AI/ML training use is permitted without licensing friction. Could not independently fetch the primary gleif.org/en/about/open-data page content directly (relied on search-result summary) — Inference flagged, but CC0 status is corroborated by multiple independent secondary sources (LEI-France, OpenOwnership).
language: English (legal names may appear in original script/language per registration authority, but reference-data schema and documentation are English).
update_frequency: Golden Copy full + delta files published 3 times daily. BIC-to-LEI mapping file updates monthly. Real-time/near-real-time updates also reflected via the API and Global LEI Index search.
fit_for_lead_prediction: High-quality but narrow-scope source: excellent, authoritative, free, and low-friction (CC0) for building a group/corporate-structure graph (parent-subsidiary links via Level 2 Relationship Records) and for entity resolution (LEI-to-ISIN/BIC/OpenCorporates linking), but coverage is limited to LEI-registered entities (skewed toward regulated/financial-market participants) and contains no deal/transaction/valuation data or acquisition events themselves. ETL effort: low — files are structured, well-documented, free, and updated 3x/day; main effort is entity-matching GLEI legal names against JCAI's target-company universe (Japanese mid-market companies likely under-represented if they lack LEIs).

name: Wikidata / DBpedia
hq_country_operator: Wikidata: operated by Wikimedia Deutschland / Wikimedia Foundation (Germany/US, non-profit). DBpedia: operated by the DBpedia Association (Germany, non-profit), extracting structured data from Wikipedia.
data_types: Structured knowledge-graph facts about companies and organizations, including ownership/corporate-structure properties: P127 'owned by' (direct owner; confirmed via wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P127, allows start-time/end-time/point-in-time/proportion qualifiers), P1830 'owner of' (inverse of P127), P749 'parent organization or unit', P355 'has subsidiary', P137 'operator', P3931 'copyright holder', P11811/P11812 'beforehand/afterward owned by' (adjacent ownership-history properties). Acquisitions are generally modeled by changing/adding P127 or P1830 statements with temporal qualifiers (P580 start time, P582 end time, P585 point in time) rather than via a dedicated 'acquisition event' item type — no evidence found of a standardized discrete 'acquisition event' item class; P1889 was referenced in the task prompt but not verified/confirmed as acquisition-relevant in this research (likely 'different from', unrelated to M&A — flag as unconfirmed). DBpedia mirrors a subset of this via Wikipedia infobox extraction into its own ontology (dbo:Organisation, dbo:Company, ~275K organizations in English DBpedia per 2026 figures).
coverage_geo: Global but sparse and skewed toward notable/publicly-documented entities (companies with Wikipedia articles or independently-created Wikidata items). Private and Asian mid-market companies are poorly covered — Inference based on known general Wikidata/DBpedia coverage bias toward English/European-language Wikipedia-notable subjects; not independently re-verified in this research pass beyond general knowledge, but consistent with DBpedia English-centric figures (English DBpedia: ~6.0M entities, 4.6M with abstracts; 275K organizations) versus Wikidata's larger but still notability-gated total.
history_depth: No fixed historical limit — items can carry qualifiers dating back to a company's founding, but actual depth/completeness depends entirely on whether contributors have added dated ownership-history statements; not systematic or guaranteed for older or private M&A events.
api: yes - SPARQL via https://query.wikidata.org/sparql (Wikidata) and equivalent DBpedia SPARQL endpoint; also Wikidata REST/Action API for entity-level access. Confirmed limits (query.wikidata.org, per Wikimedia documentation found via search): 60-second hard query timeout; rate limiting buckets by User-Agent+IP, allowing 60 seconds of cumulative processing time per 60-second window and 30 error-queries/minute; exceeding limits returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header, repeated violations escalate to a temporary or longer ban (HTTP 403); clients must send an identifiable User-Agent with contact info per the User-Agent policy or risk being blocked outright.
bulk_delivery: Yes - Wikidata publishes full JSON dumps (one JSON entity object per line) at dumps.wikimedia.org, roughly every few days/weekly; compressed dump size has grown from ~3.3GB (2014) to an estimated ~90GB compressed / ~500GB+ uncompressed by recent years (figures from secondary sources/research figures, not independently fetched from the official dump page in this pass — Inference flagged for exact current size). DBpedia publishes periodic full dataset releases (N-Triples/Turtle RDF dumps) via downloads.dbpedia.org and the DBpedia Databus.
pricing: Free (both Wikidata and DBpedia are free, open, non-profit-operated resources with no paid tiers).
ml_training_license: Wikidata: CC0 (public domain dedication) confirmed via wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing — all structured data in main/Property/Lexeme/EntitySchema namespaces is CC0, explicitly to maximize reuse including by commercial/AI products; attribution-requiring content is disallowed from being added to Wikidata precisely to preserve this. AI training is permitted with no license friction. DBpedia: dual-licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 + GFDL 1.1 (since release 3.4, matching Wikipedia's own licensing) — this is a share-alike/attribution license, meaning derived datasets that are redistributed may need to carry the same license and attribution; whether an internally-trained (non-redistributed) ML model triggers this obligation is unclear/untested - Inference: for internal-only model training without redistributing the DBpedia dataset itself, ShareAlike is less likely to bite, but this is not a legal conclusion and should be checked with counsel given the org's stated policy of deferring legal/licensing judgments to qualified professionals.
language: Multilingual; labels/descriptions available in Japanese and English among ~300 languages for Wikidata items. English-language Wikipedia/DBpedia has by far the deepest company coverage; Japanese DBpedia (ja.dbpedia.org) exists but is comparatively much smaller - Inference based on general known DBpedia language-edition size disparities, not independently re-verified here.
update_frequency: Wikidata: continuously edited live (via SPARQL/API you get current state); full JSON dumps produced roughly weekly/every few days. DBpedia: periodic dataset releases tied to DBpedia extraction-framework runs against Wikipedia dumps (historically annual-ish major releases plus a 'live' sync extension in some deployments) — exact current DBpedia release cadence not independently confirmed in this pass.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Low-to-moderate fit as a primary source: free, CC0/well-licensed (Wikidata), and useful for enriching a known-entity graph with parent/subsidiary/ownership links and for cross-referencing identifiers, but coverage is sparse and notability-biased — most private and Asian (especially Japanese) mid-market companies that would be actual M&A targets are simply absent, and neither source records deal values, deal dates as structured 'acquisition transactions', or financial metrics needed for target prediction. ETL effort: low for the data that does exist (clean SPARQL/dump access) but yields limited incremental coverage for JCAI's likely target universe — best used as a supplementary enrichment/cross-linking layer (e.g., resolving parent-company hierarchies for large/public acquirers) rather than a core training dataset.

name: GDELT Project (Events Database + Global Knowledge Graph)
hq_country_operator: USA — independent open-data project created by Kalev H. Leetaru; distributed via Google Cloud/BigQuery public-dataset infrastructure (gdelt-bq)
data_types: Two core layers verified via direct fetch: (1) Event Database — CAMEO-coded event records (300+ political/diplomatic/conflict categories). VERIFIED via the official CAMEO event-code list that CAMEO is a political/military-conflict taxonomy (cooperation, protest, sanctions, force, negotiation) and contains NO merger/acquisition or corporate-transaction code — a third-party commercial product called 'CAMEO+' (docs.gdeltcloud.com, not the free GDELT taxonomy) does add a corporate 'CO01 M&A' code, but that is a separate paid layer, not the standard free CAMEO scheme GDELT itself uses. (2) Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) — themes, people/org/location entities, tone/sentiment (GCAM), counts. VERIFIED against the full public GKG theme list (~13,000 themes, mirrored on GitHub CatoMinor/GDELT-GKG-Themes) that there is NO ECON_MERGER, ECON_ACQUISITION, MERGER, ACQUISITION, TAKEOVER, or CORPORATE theme; the closest adjacent ECON_* themes that do exist are ECON_BANKRUPTCY, ECON_MOU (memorandum of understanding), ECON_IPO, ECON_MONOPOLY, ECON_STOCKMARKET, ECON_FOREIGNINVEST, ECON_ENTREPRENEURSHIP. GDELT also does not redistribute full article text — only metadata/entities/sentiment plus the source article URL.
coverage_geo: Global; news monitored in 65 live machine-translated languages plus ~35 additional sample-translated languages (GDELT 2.0 documentation)
history_depth: GDELT 1.0 Event Database: Jan 1, 1979–present (daily updates). GDELT 1.0 GKG: begins Apr 1, 2013. GDELT 2.0 Events + GKG 2.0: begins Feb 19, 2015 (confirmed via GDELT project blog post 'GDELT 2.0: Our Global World in Realtime'), updated every 15 minutes continuously to present; 250M+ total event records cited on the GDELT About page.
api: yes — BigQuery public dataset 'gdelt-bq' (e.g. gdelt-bq.full.events, gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg) queryable with standard SQL; also a GDELT DOC 2.0 article-search API.
